parts.text: Which claim correctly names the ray?

options.text: Ray $PQ$ or ray $PR$, because the starting point $P$ comes first, then a point on the path.
Ray $QP$, because $Q$ and $P$ both lie on the path.
Line $PQR$, treating the path as a two-way line with no starting point.
Ray $RP$, reading the letters from the far end back toward $P$.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

stem: Alok draws a ray that starts at point $P$ and passes through points $Q$ and $R$ in that order.

part_answers.answer: A ray is named with its endpoint first, then any other labelled point on its path in the direction of extension, so PQ and PR both name the same ray from P through Q and R.

teacher.key_rationale: Endpoint P must lead the name; QP and RP reverse that order, and calling it line PQR drops the ray's starting point.
